1.english_reference: Whither is thy beloved gone , O thou fairest among women ?

traditions.WLC: אָ֚נָה הָלַ֣ךְ דּוֹדֵ֔ ךְ הַ יָּפָ֖ה בַּ נָּשִׁ֑ים
traditions.VUL: Quo ábiit diléctus tuus , o pulchérrima mulíerum ?
traditions.KJV: Whither is thy beloved gone , O thou fairest among women ?

1.english_reference: whither is thy beloved turned aside ?

traditions.WLC: אָ֚נָה פָּנָ֣ה דוֹדֵ֔ ךְ
traditions.VUL: quo declinávit diléctus tuus ,
traditions.KJV: whither is thy beloved turned aside ?

1.english_reference: that we may seek him with thee .

traditions.WLC: וּ נְבַקְשֶׁ֖ נּוּ עִמָּֽ ךְ
traditions.VUL: et quærémus eum tecum ?
traditions.KJV: that we may seek him with thee .

traditions.LXX: Ἀδελφός μου κατέβη εἰς κῆπον αὐτοῦ εἰς φιάλας τοῦ ἀρώματος , ποιμαίνειν ἐν κήποις καὶ συλλέγειν κρίνα .

2.english_reference: My beloved is gone down into his garden , to the beds of spices ,

traditions.WLC: דּוֹדִ י֙ יָרַ֣ד לְ גַנּ֔ וֹ לַ עֲרוּג֖וֹת הַ בֹּ֑שֶׂם
traditions.VUL: Diléctus meus descéndit in hortum suum ad aréolam arómatum ,
traditions.KJV: My beloved is gone down into his garden , to the beds of spices ,

traditions.WLC: לִ רְעוֹת֙ בַּ גַּנִּ֔ים
traditions.VUL: ut pascátur in hortis ,
traditions.KJV: to feed in the gardens ,

traditions.WLC: וְ לִ לְקֹ֖ט שֽׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים
traditions.VUL: et lília cólligat .
traditions.KJV: and to gather lilies .

traditions.LXX: ἐγὼ τῷ ἀδελφιδῷ μου καὶ ἀδελφιδός μου ἐμοί , ὁ ποιμαίνων ἐν τοῖς κρίνοις .

3.english_reference: I [ am ] my beloved ’s , and my beloved [ is ] mine :

traditions.WLC: אֲנִ֤י לְ דוֹדִ י֙ וְ דוֹדִ֣ י לִ֔ י
traditions.VUL: Ego dilécto meo , et diléctus meus mihi ,
traditions.KJV: I [ am ] my beloved ’s , and my beloved [ is ] mine :

traditions.WLC: הָ רֹעֶ֖ה בַּ שׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים
traditions.VUL: qui páscitur inter lília .
traditions.KJV: he feedeth among the lilies .

traditions.LXX: Καλὴ εἶ πλησίον μου , ὡς εὐδοκία , ὡραία ὡς Ἰερουσαλήμ , θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναι .

4.english_reference: Thou [ art ] beautiful , O my love , as Tirzah ,

traditions.WLC: יָפָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ רַעְיָתִ י֙ כְּ תִרְצָ֔ה
traditions.VUL: Pulchra es amíca mea , suávis ,
traditions.KJV: Thou [ art ] beautiful , O my love , as Tirzah ,

traditions.WLC: נָאוָ֖ה כִּ ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם
traditions.VUL: et decóra sicut Ierúsalem :
traditions.KJV: comely as Jerusalem ,

4.english_reference: terrible as [ an army ] with banners .

traditions.WLC: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּ נִּדְגָּלֽוֹת
traditions.VUL: terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta .
traditions.KJV: terrible as [ an army ] with banners .

traditions.LXX: ἀπόστρεψον ὀφθαλμούς σου ἀπεναντίον μου , ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἀνεπτέρωσάν με . τρίχωμά σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν αἰγῶν αἳ ἀνεφάνησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ Γαλαάδ ,

5.english_reference: Turn away thine eyes from me , for they have overcome me :

traditions.WLC: הָסֵ֤בִּי עֵינַ֨יִ ךְ֙ מִ נֶּגְדִּ֔ י שֶׁ֥ הֵ֖ם הִרְהִיבֻ֑ נִי
traditions.VUL: Avérte óculos tuos a me , quia ipsi me avoláre fecérunt .
traditions.KJV: Turn away thine eyes from me , for they have overcome me :

5.english_reference: thy hair [ is ] as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead .

traditions.WLC: שַׂעְרֵ ךְ֙ כְּ עֵ֣דֶר הָֽ עִזִּ֔ים שֶׁ גָּלְשׁ֖וּ מִן הַ גִּלְעָֽד
traditions.VUL: Capílli tui sicut grex caprárum , quæ apparuérunt de Gálaad .
traditions.KJV: thy hair [ is ] as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead .

traditions.LXX: ὀδόντες σου ὡς ἀγέλαι τῶν κεκαρμένων αἳ ἀνέβησαν ἀπὸ τοῦ λουτροῦ , αἱ πᾶσαι διδυμεύουσαι , καὶ ἀτεκνοῦσα οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐταῖς . ὡς σπαρτίον τὸ κόκκινον χείλη σου , καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὡραία .

6.english_reference: Thy teeth [ are ] as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing ,

traditions.WLC: שִׁנַּ֨יִ ךְ֙ כְּ עֵ֣דֶר הָֽ רְחֵלִ֔ים שֶׁ עָל֖וּ מִן הָ רַחְצָ֑ה
traditions.VUL: Dentes tui sicut grex óvium , quæ ascendérunt de lavácro :
traditions.KJV: Thy teeth [ are ] as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing ,

traditions.WLC: שֶׁ כֻּלָּ ם֙ מַתְאִימ֔וֹת
traditions.VUL: omnes geméllis fœ́tibus ,
traditions.KJV: whereof every one beareth twins ,

6.english_reference: and [ there is ] not one barren among them .

traditions.WLC: וְ שַׁכֻּלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין בָּ הֶֽם
traditions.VUL: et stérilis non est in eis .
traditions.KJV: and [ there is ] not one barren among them .

traditions.LXX: ὡς λέπυρον ῥόας μῆλόν σου ἐκτὸς τῆς σιωπήσεώς σου .

7.english_reference: As a piece of a pomegranate [ are ] thy temples within thy locks .

traditions.WLC: כְּ פֶ֤לַח הָ רִמּוֹן֙ רַקָּתֵ֔ ךְ מִ בַּ֖עַד לְ צַמָּתֵֽ ךְ
traditions.VUL: Sicut cortex mali púnici , sic genæ tuæ absque occúltis tuis .
traditions.KJV: As a piece of a pomegranate [ are ] thy temples within thy locks .

traditions.LXX: ἑξήκοντά εἰσιν βασίλισσαι , ὀγδοήκοντα παλλακαί , καὶ νεάνιδες ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός ·

8.english_reference: There are threescore queens , and fourscore concubines ,

traditions.WLC: שִׁשִּׁ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ מְּלָכ֔וֹת וּ שְׁמֹנִ֖ים פִּֽילַגְשִׁ֑ים
traditions.VUL: Sexagínta sunt regínæ , et octogínta concubínæ ,
traditions.KJV: There are threescore queens , and fourscore concubines ,

traditions.WLC: וַ עֲלָמ֖וֹת אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר
traditions.VUL: et adolescentulárum non est númerus .
traditions.KJV: and virgins without number .

traditions.LXX: μία ἐστὶν περιστερά μου , τελεία μου , μία ἐστὶν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς , ἐκλεκτή ἐστιν τῇ τεκούσῃ αὐτῆς . εἴδοσαν αὐτὴν θυγατέρες καὶ μακαριοῦσιν αὐτήν , βασίλισσαι καί γε παλλακαί , καὶ αἰνέσουσιν αὐτήν .

9.english_reference: My dove , my undefiled is [ but ] one ;

traditions.WLC: אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ יוֹנָתִ֣ י תַמָּתִ֔ י
traditions.VUL: Una est colúmba mea , perfécta mea ,
traditions.KJV: My dove , my undefiled is [ but ] one ;

9.english_reference: she [ is ] the [ only ] one of her mother , she [ is ] the choice [ one ] of her that bare her .

traditions.WLC: אַחַ֥ת הִיא֙ לְ אִמָּ֔ הּ בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְ יֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑ הּ
traditions.VUL: una est matris suæ , elécta genetríci suæ .
traditions.KJV: she [ is ] the [ only ] one of her mother , she [ is ] the choice [ one ] of her that bare her .

9.english_reference: The daughters saw her , and blessed her ;

traditions.WLC: רָא֤וּ הָ בָנוֹת֙ וַֽ יְאַשְּׁר֔וּ
traditions.VUL: Vidérunt eam fíliæ , et beatíssimam prædicavérunt :
traditions.KJV: The daughters saw her , and blessed her ; [ yea ] ,

9.english_reference: [ yea ] , the queens and the concubines , and they praised her .

traditions.WLC: הָ מְלָכ֥וֹת וּ פִֽילַגְשִׁ֖ים וַֽ יְהַלְלֽוּ הָ
traditions.VUL: regínæ et concubínæ , et laudavérunt eam .
traditions.KJV: the queens and the concubines , and they praised her .

traditions.LXX: Τίς αὕτη ἡ ἐκκύπτουσα ὡσεὶ ὄρθρος , καλὴ ὡς σελήνη , ἐκλεκτὴ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος , θάμβος ὡς τεταγμέναι ;

10.english_reference: Who [ is ] she [ that ] looketh forth as the morning ,

traditions.WLC: מִי זֹ֥את הַ נִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה כְּמוֹ שָׁ֑חַר
traditions.VUL: Quæ est ista , quæ progréditur quasi auróra consúrgens ,
traditions.KJV: Who [ is ] she [ that ] looketh forth as the morning ,

10.english_reference: fair as the moon , clear as the sun ,

traditions.WLC: יָפָ֣ה כַ לְּבָנָ֗ה בָּרָה֙ כַּֽ חַמָּ֔ה
traditions.VUL: pulchra ut luna , elécta ut sol ,
traditions.KJV: fair as the moon , clear as the sun , [ and ]

10.english_reference: [ and ] terrible as [ an army ] with banners ?

traditions.WLC: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּ נִּדְגָּלֽוֹת
traditions.VUL: terríbilis ut castrórum ácies ordináta ?
traditions.KJV: terrible as [ an army ] with banners ?

traditions.LXX: Εἰς κῆπον καρύας κατέβην ἰδεῖν ἐν γενήμασιν τοῦ χειμάρρου , ἰδεῖν εἰ ἤνθησεν ἡ ἄμπελος , ἐξήνθησαν αἱ ῥόαι · ἐκεῖ δώσω τοὺς μαστούς μου σοί .
